newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica seen rebounding after results.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica seen rebounding after results.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Telefonica extended early losses on Friday after posting nine-month results in line with analysts' forecasts, but the stock was seen rebounding on the firm's healthy earnings, dealers said.
"These came in bang on target and after the (stock's) sharp rise in the past few days we've seen it come off a little on the news," said a trader at a Madrid brokerage.

"The company gives a lot of information in advance of results so everything's very much in the price. But with the (early 1997) placement coming up we should see it go up a little. I think it'll end the year just under 3,000 pesetas," the trader added.
At 1310 GMT Telefonica was down 20 pesetas, 0.72 percent, to 2,770 while the Ibex-35 index was down 0.01 percent to 4,492.35.
One analyst highlighted the quality of the firm's nine-month earnings, which rose 19.8 percent to 102.23 billion pesetas.

"The results are good. You can see that operating profit has risen, but at a greater rate than in the previous quarter. It's up eight percent at this point versus an increase of 4.5 percent last time around," said Javier Borrachero, telecoms analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa.
Operating profit rose to 413.99 billion pesetas in the nine months to end-September on a 13.3 percent improvement in operating income.
He saw upside for the shares medium term on the back of an expected 20 percent rise in earnings both in 1996 and in 1997.
"It's one of the best stocks in Spain, with a rising income stream and falling financial costs. It clearly has potential," he added.
Financial costs fell 15.4 percent to September on the back of a 2.7 percent fall in debt, helped by lower Spanish interest rates, Telefonica said in a note accompanying the results.
In the short term the stock's rise had been "somewhat exaggerated," Borrachero said, ahead of the public offering of the government's remaining 21 percent stake in the firm, set for early 1997.

Speculation that one brokerage in particular has been buying shares for a final client ahead of the placement has been rife, with strong demand powering the share price to ever more dizzying heights in recent weeks.
Since the start of October, Telefonica has risen about 22 percent to Thursday's close at 2,790 pesetas. In the same period the Ibex-35 index of major stocks has risen around six percent.
